text:
Maya: Kicking off an experiment to tune continuous batching via a windowed queue + token steering for p95 SLOs. Want to trade small avg cost increase for stable p95 across routes/tiers.
Ryan: Nice. What's the window size and steering rule?
Maya: Starting with 50ms window, max microbatch tokens 128, steer token budget per route based on recent 1m p95. If p95 > target, reduce budget by 15% for that route.
Alex: Data from yesterday's perf run shows kernel swap count spikes when budgets drop quickly — that caused a transient p95 regression on long-chat. We should smooth changes.
Sanjay: Agreed. Suggest exponential smoothing on budget changes (alpha = 0.25) and a minimum cooldown of 30s before applying further reductions.
Ryan: I ran a quick profile: before tweak: p95 long-chat=152ms, kv_hit=0.78, avg_microbatch_tokens=8. After naive steering: p95 long-chat=210ms, kv_hit=0.71, avg_microbatch_tokens=12, kernel_switches+450%. Looks like larger microbatches plus kernel churn.
Maya: Important signal — the steering increased microbatch size (good for throughput) but pushed sequences into a different kernel path causing warmup spikes. Need to bias steering to avoid crossing kernel-prefetch thresholds.
Alex: Can we add a kernel-aware margin? i.e., if route's avg_seq_len crosses kernel_threshold (e.g. 256 tokens) apply additional 10 token headroom.
Sanjay: I'll prototype a policy that attaches a small kernel margin and enforces kv-prefetch affinity: prefer budgets that keep requests on same kernel for at least 200ms.
perf-bot: deploy-report: canary profile run #34 finished. p95 overall +8ms, long-chat p95 +58ms, short-chat -3ms. kv_hit delta -0.06.
Maya: Thanks perf-bot. That confirms. Proposal: implement smoothing + kernel-margin + 30s cooldown, and route-tier overrides: premium: +20 token headroom, standard: no extra, internal: -10 token cap (to save cost).
Ryan: I like tiered headroom. Also add a soft cap on avg_microbatch_tokens increase per minute (e.g., +3 tokens/min) to prevent sudden jumps.
Alex: For observability, let's track these in a dashboard: route_p95, kv_hit_rate, avg_microbatch_tokens, kernel_switch_rate, budget_change_rate. Create alerts: route_p95 > target by 10% for 3min, kernel_switch_rate spike > 2x baseline.
Sanjay: Quick implementation note: plugin config looks like
```
steering:
  window_ms: 50
  smoothing_alpha: 0.25
  cooldown_s: 30
  per_route_margins:
    premium: 20
    standard: 0
    internal: -10
  max_tokens_delta_per_min: 3
  kernel_affinity_ms: 200
```
Ryan: Can we canary on 5% of traffic for 1 hour with sampling by route (spread across premium/standard)?
Maya: Yes. Canary plan: 5% traffic, sample by route so we see long-chat exposure, run for 60m, watch the dashboard metrics and rollback if long-chat p95 increases > 15% or kv_hit drops > 0.08.
deploy-bot: canary-started: id=canary-2026-03-18-01 route-split=per-route-sample pct=5 duration=60m
Alex: One more thing — kernel selection telemetry isn't surfaced in the route dashboards. I'll add kernel_switch_rate and kernel_warmup_ms per route.
Maya: Action items: Sanjay implement policy + config, Alex add kernel metrics to dashboards, Ryan run canary and monitor, I'll own rollback criteria and postmortem if needed.
Ryan: On it. Will update in this thread with hourly snapshots. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks team — priority is keeping p95 SLOs stable. Small extra cost is fine as long as we avoid kernel-induced spikes.
